reason: The arterial wall has an unlined inside, and the lining cells fit there, so this looks like a useful start on the artery goal.
expectation: I expect a lined artery with a strong, elastic wall; I’m not sure whether that completes the goal.

alternatives.reason: The capillaries and body cells also clearly fit the exchange goal, but I chose to start with the outward route.
The vein also needs a lining, but I chose the artery first.

effect: The lined arterial vessels complete the outward-route goal; next I can build the exchange route.
reaction: The arrows made the artery’s direction clear.
reason: The thin capillaries belong near body cells for exchanging materials.
expectation: I expect capillaries positioned beside the cells, ready for exchange; I’m not sure how much exchange the result will show.

alternatives.reason: The vein also needs a lining, but I want to follow the route outward to the cells first.

effect: The capillary bed completes the exchange goal and shows materials crossing while blood cells stay inside.
reaction: Seeing oxygen and nutrients go out while carbon dioxide goes in makes the exchange clearer.
reason: The venous wall needs a lining, so I’ll prepare the return route next.
expectation: I expect a lined vein; it may still need the one-way valve flaps.

alternatives.reason: I could connect the arteries to the capillaries now, but I want to prepare the return route first.

effect: The veins now have a lining and point toward the heart; they still need valves for the return-route goal.
reaction: The arrows make the return direction clear.
reason: The valve flaps fit the veins and should help prevent backward flow.
expectation: I expect veins with one-way valves that open for forward flow and close against backward flow.

alternatives.reason: Connecting arteries to capillaries also follows the blood route, but I want to finish preparing the veins first.

effect: The valves complete the return route, and the picture shows muscle squeezing helping move blood forward. The three routes now need joining.
reaction: The muscle squeeze was a useful detail I hadn't expected.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it starts joining the outward route to the exchange vessels.
expectation: I expect the arteries to connect to the capillary bed; the venous return may still need to be joined afterward.

effect: The artery now branches into capillaries, leaving open ends for the return route.
reaction: The branching picture makes the connection clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the venous return fits the open collecting ends.
expectation: I expect the veins to connect to the capillaries, completing the route back toward the heart.

effect: The completed network connects arteries, capillaries and veins into a route away from and back toward the heart.
reaction: The continuous arrow makes the whole route easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the capillary bed was most worthwhile because it showed what moves between blood and body cells, and that blood cells stay inside.

leastWorthwhile.text: Lining the artery and vein felt a little repetitive, even though the arrows helped distinguish their directions.

surprise.text: I didn't expect the picture to show a contracting muscle squeezing a vein while its valves guide blood forward.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary: the pictures showed where the parts fit and what they did, although the final connections were the only offered combinations.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter to see how the connected body systems work together; the exchange and vein-valve pictures made this chapter interesting.
